database_summary: Chinook-like music store schema in SQLite. Core entities: Artist, Album, Track, Genre, MediaType, Playlist. Customer and Employee represent people; Invoice and InvoiceLine are billing events (transactions). Tables are small-to-medium (rows range Album 347..Track 3503). Foreign keys link Artist->Album->Track and Track->(Genre,MediaType) and Track<->Playlist via PlaylistTrack. Invoice/InvoiceLine link customers to purchased tracks. No temporal history/versioning columns beyond datetime invoice/employee dates. Many-to-many relationships (Playlist-Track) and one-to-many (Album->Track, Invoice->InvoiceLine) present; joins may multiply rows when bridging many-to-many or joining facts to dimensional entities.

accepted.name: track_with_dimensions
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  Track.TrackId AS TrackId,
  Track.Name AS Name,
  Track.AlbumId AS AlbumId,
  Album.Title AS Title,
  Album.ArtistId AS ArtistId,
  Artist.Name AS Name_artist,
  Track.MediaTypeId AS MediaTypeId,
  MediaType.Name AS Name_mediaType,
  Track.GenreId AS GenreId,
  Genre.Name AS Name_genre,
  Track.Composer AS Composer,
  Track.Milliseconds AS Milliseconds,
  Track.Bytes AS Bytes,
  Track.UnitPrice AS UnitPrice
FROM Track
LEFT JOIN Album ON Track.AlbumId = Album.AlbumId
LEFT JOIN Artist ON Album.ArtistId = Artist.ArtistId
LEFT JOIN Genre ON Track.GenreId = Genre.GenreId
LEFT JOIN MediaType ON Track.MediaTypeId = MediaType.MediaTypeId
accepted.description: Denormalized track-level relation joined to Album, Artist, Genre, and MediaType. Use this when analyses need track attributes together with album/artist/genre/media descriptors (e.g., catalog reports, sales joined to track metadata). | Use for: List tracks with album/artist/genre/media metadata; Compare track attributes by genre or artist; Enrich invoice-line sales with track metadata

accepted.name: invoice_line_with_track_and_invoice
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  InvoiceLine.InvoiceLineId AS InvoiceLineId,
  InvoiceLine.InvoiceId AS InvoiceId,
  Invoice.CustomerId AS CustomerId,
  Invoice.InvoiceDate AS InvoiceDate,
  Invoice.BillingCountry AS BillingCountry,
  InvoiceLine.TrackId AS TrackId,
  Track.Name AS Name,
  Track.AlbumId AS AlbumId,
  Album.ArtistId AS ArtistId,
  Artist.Name AS Name_artist,
  InvoiceLine.UnitPrice AS UnitPrice,
  InvoiceLine.Quantity AS Quantity,
  (InvoiceLine.UnitPrice * InvoiceLine.Quantity) AS LineTotal
FROM InvoiceLine
LEFT JOIN Invoice ON InvoiceLine.InvoiceId = Invoice.InvoiceId
LEFT JOIN Track ON InvoiceLine.TrackId = Track.TrackId
LEFT JOIN Album ON Track.AlbumId = Album.AlbumId
LEFT JOIN Artist ON Album.ArtistId = Artist.ArtistId
accepted.description: InvoiceLine rows augmented with Invoice and Track/Album/Artist basic metadata and computed line revenue. Useful for revenue, quantity and order-level analyses at the invoice-line grain. | Use for: Compute revenue by track/artist/album/customer; Analyze quantity and price mixes on invoice lines; Join sales to track metadata for catalog performance

accepted.name: album_track_counts
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  Album.AlbumId AS AlbumId,
  Album.Title AS Title,
  Album.ArtistId AS ArtistId,
  COUNT(Track.TrackId) AS TrackCount,
  SUM(Track.Milliseconds) AS TotalMilliseconds,
  SUM(Track.Bytes) AS TotalBytes,
  AVG(Track.UnitPrice) AS AvgUnitPrice
FROM Album
LEFT JOIN Track ON Album.AlbumId = Track.AlbumId
GROUP BY Album.AlbumId, Album.Title, Album.ArtistId
accepted.description: Per-album aggregated measures: number of tracks, total duration (milliseconds), total bytes, average track price. Use for album-level summaries and ranking albums by size/duration/value. | Use for: Which albums have the most tracks or longest total duration?; Average price per track by album; Album size summaries for catalog management

accepted.name: customer_invoice_aggregates
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  Customer.CustomerId AS CustomerId,
  Customer.FirstName AS FirstName,
  Customer.LastName AS LastName,
  COUNT(Invoice.InvoiceId) AS InvoiceCount,
  SUM(Invoice.Total) AS LifetimeTotal,
  AVG(Invoice.Total) AS AvgInvoiceTotal,
  MAX(Invoice.InvoiceDate) AS LastInvoiceDate
FROM Customer
LEFT JOIN Invoice ON Customer.CustomerId = Invoice.CustomerId
GROUP BY Customer.CustomerId, Customer.FirstName, Customer.LastName
accepted.description: Per-customer invoice-level aggregates: number of invoices, total lifetime spend, average invoice total, last invoice date. Useful for customer lifetime value and recency/frequency/monetary (RFM) analyses. | Use for: Compute customer lifetime value and recency; Segment customers by spend or invoice frequency; Find most recent invoices per customer

accepted.name: artist_album_counts
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  Artist.ArtistId AS ArtistId,
  Artist.Name AS Name,
  COUNT(DISTINCT Album.AlbumId) AS AlbumCount,
  COUNT(Track.TrackId) AS TrackCount
FROM Artist
LEFT JOIN Album ON Artist.ArtistId = Album.ArtistId
LEFT JOIN Track ON Album.AlbumId = Track.AlbumId
GROUP BY Artist.ArtistId, Artist.Name
accepted.description: Per-artist aggregate: number of albums and number of tracks across all their albums. Use for artist catalog size and productivity comparisons. | Use for: Rank artists by number of albums or tracks; Catalog coverage by artist

accepted.name: track_popularity_rank_within_artist
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  t.TrackId AS TrackId,
  t.Name AS Name,
  a.ArtistId AS ArtistId,
  a.Name AS Name_artist,
  SUM(il.Quantity) AS TotalQuantity,
  SUM(il.UnitPrice * il.Quantity) AS TotalRevenue,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY a.ArtistId ORDER BY SUM(il.Quantity) DESC) AS RankByQuantity,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY a.ArtistId ORDER BY SUM(il.UnitPrice * il.Quantity) DESC) AS RankByRevenue
FROM InvoiceLine il
LEFT JOIN Track t ON il.TrackId = t.TrackId
LEFT JOIN Album al ON t.AlbumId = al.AlbumId
LEFT JOIN Artist a ON al.ArtistId = a.ArtistId
GROUP BY t.TrackId, t.Name, a.ArtistId, a.Name
accepted.description: Ranks tracks for each artist by total sold quantity and revenue (derived from InvoiceLine). Useful for Top-K track queries per artist or artist catalog leaders. Exposes rank columns so callers can filter by rank <= K downstream. | Use for: Top-N tracks per artist by units sold or revenue; Identify a band's best-selling tracks

accepted.name: invoices_running_total_by_customer
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  Invoice.InvoiceId AS InvoiceId,
  Invoice.CustomerId AS CustomerId,
  Invoice.InvoiceDate AS InvoiceDate,
  Invoice.Total AS Total,
  SUM(Invoice.Total) OVER (PARTITION BY Invoice.CustomerId ORDER BY Invoice.InvoiceDate ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS RunningTotal
FROM Invoice
accepted.description: Invoice-level running total per customer ordered by InvoiceDate. Useful for analyzing cumulative spend over time per customer and identifying spend milestones. Exposes a running_total column for downstream thresholds. | Use for: Show cumulative customer spend over time; Find when customers crossed spend thresholds

accepted.name: playlist_track_enriched
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  PlaylistTrack.PlaylistId AS PlaylistId,
  Playlist.Name AS Name_playlist,
  PlaylistTrack.TrackId AS TrackId,
  Track.Name AS Name,
  Track.AlbumId AS AlbumId,
  Album.ArtistId AS ArtistId,
  Artist.Name AS Name_artist
FROM PlaylistTrack
LEFT JOIN Playlist ON PlaylistTrack.PlaylistId = Playlist.PlaylistId
LEFT JOIN Track ON PlaylistTrack.TrackId = Track.TrackId
LEFT JOIN Album ON Track.AlbumId = Album.AlbumId
LEFT JOIN Artist ON Album.ArtistId = Artist.ArtistId
accepted.description: PlaylistTrack bridge rows enriched with Playlist, Track, Album and Artist metadata. Useful for playlist content reports and analyzing which artists/albums appear in playlists. | Use for: List tracks in playlists with artist/album info; Which artists appear most often across playlists

accepted.name: genre_sales_aggregates
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  g.GenreId AS GenreId,
  g.Name AS Name,
  SUM(il.Quantity) AS TotalQuantity,
  SUM(il.UnitPrice * il.Quantity) AS TotalRevenue,
  COUNT(DISTINCT t.TrackId) AS DistinctTrackCount
FROM InvoiceLine il
LEFT JOIN Track t ON il.TrackId = t.TrackId
LEFT JOIN Genre g ON t.GenreId = g.GenreId
GROUP BY g.GenreId, g.Name
accepted.description: Aggregates of sales by genre (units and revenue) by joining InvoiceLine -> Track -> Genre. Useful for genre-level performance and trend analyses. | Use for: Rank genres by revenue or units sold; Understand breadth of tracks sold per genre
